stories.headline: US Commerce Secretary Lutnick tells ASML one of its EUV machines may be in China; ASML denies

key_facts.fact: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told ASML's senior leaders in a series of recent meetings that one of its top-of-the-line EUV lithography machines may have made its way into China in violation of US-led export restrictions.
key_facts.excerpt: In a series of recent meetings, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick outlined concerns to ASML's senior leaders that one of its top-of-the-line machines may have made its way into China, in violation of US-led export restrictions.

key_facts.fact: ASML has never been allowed to ship EUV systems to China because of curbs imposed during the first Trump administration; EUV is used by TSMC to manufacture processors for Nvidia and Apple.
key_facts.excerpt: EUV systems are used by firms such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. to manufacture processors for the likes of Nvidia Corp. and Apple Inc., and ASML has never been allowed to ship them to China because of curbs imposed during the first Trump administration.

key_facts.fact: ASML denies the claim, saying the tools are the size of a school bus, manufactured in limited quantities, and require constant upkeep from ASML employees — and that no EUV machine is in China.
key_facts.excerpt: ASML has pushed back on Lutnick's suggestion, explaining that none of these tools — which are the size of a school bus, are manufactured in limited quantities, and require constant upkeep from ASML employees — are in China.

key_facts.fact: Senior US officials say they have evidence ASML shipped EUV-related components and transport equipment to China but have repeatedly declined to share it with Bloomberg or ASML; ASML circulated a document in Washington in April titled 'No indication of any ASML EUV System in China'.
key_facts.excerpt: Senior administration officials told Bloomberg they have evidence that ASML shipped EUV-related components and transport equipment to China, though they've declined, repeatedly, to show it — to Bloomberg or, apparently, to ASML itself.

key_facts.fact: A bipartisan US bill (MATCH Act) introduced in April 2026 would ban all ASML DUV shipments to China, going beyond the existing EUV ban; DUV currently accounts for roughly a fifth of ASML's expected 2026 revenue, and China's share of system sales fell from 36% to 19% in Q1 2026 due to stricter controls.
key_facts.excerpt: In April 2026, U.S. lawmakers introduced the MATCH Act, a bill that would also ban the export of DUV immersion machines and the servicing of existing machines in China. China recently accounted for 36 percent of system sales, but that share dropped to 19 percent in the first quarter of 2026 due to stricter controls.

stories.headline: Google guarantees $3.2B to fund NY data center that will rent its TPUs to Anthropic

key_facts.fact: Google provided a $3.2 billion financial guarantee to fund a New York data center that will rent its tensor processing units (TPUs) to Anthropic, mirroring Nvidia's playbook of underwriting customer demand for its chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Google provided a $3.2 billion financial guarantee for the project to boost its AI chip game and challenge NVIDIA's lead. The company is backing Anthropic by powering its work with Google's own TPUs (tensor processing units) at a huge New York data center, pretty much mirroring how NVIDIA encourages demand for its GPUs.

key_facts.fact: Google plans to sell TPUs more directly to outside customers and has rolled out a new chip; some clients are seeing up to 30% cost savings and 4x performance versus alternatives, with Google planning to raise $85 billion for more AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Google isn't stopping there: it's now planning to sell TPUs directly to more customers and has rolled out a new chip designed for faster, cheaper AI processing. Some clients are already seeing up to 30% cost savings and four times the speed. Plus, Google plans to raise $85 billion for even more AI infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic earlier disclosed an April 2026 deal with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity starting in 2027; Claude's run-rate revenue reached $30 billion in 2026, up from about $9 billion at end of 2025, with 1,000+ business customers each spending over $1 million annually.
key_facts.excerpt: We have signed a new agreement with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity that we expect to come online starting in 2027. Our run-rate revenue has now surpassed $30 billion—up from approximately $9 billion at the end of 2025. Today that number exceeds 1,000, doubling in less than two months.

key_facts.fact: Google has previously contracted to sell three million TPUs to Intel for production beginning in 2028 and is in talks with Samsung for its next-gen 'Icefish' 10th-gen TPU and Axion processors, signaling a broader push to diversify foundry sourcing as it scales its custom-silicon business.
key_facts.excerpt: Google is discussing two separate Samsung engagements. One covers its next-generation Axion processors expected around 2028, while the other involves components tied to its 10th-generation Tensor Processing Unit, codenamed Icefish, which is being co-developed with MediaTek.

stories.headline: Intel hires former SK Hynix CEO Seok-Hee Lee as EVP to lead Intel Foundry advanced packaging

key_facts.fact: Intel announced on June 18 the appointment of Seok-Hee Lee as executive vice president of Intel Foundry, reporting directly to CEO Lip-Bu Tan, to lead advanced packaging, system integration, back-end technology development, and back-end manufacturing.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel Corporation today announced the appointment of Seok-Hee Lee as executive vice president of Intel Foundry, reporting directly to CEO Lip-Bu Tan. In this role, Lee will lead all advanced packaging, system integration, back-end technology development, and back-end manufacturing.

key_facts.fact: Lee will scale advanced packaging technologies into high-volume manufacturing, including EMIB-T (Intel's 2.5D packaging) and High-Density Hybrid Bonding (HBI), a next-generation 3D packaging process; Navid Shahriari, who had been responsible for packaging, will retire.
key_facts.excerpt: Lee will be responsible for scaling advanced packaging technologies into high-volume manufacturing, including Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge-T (EMIB-T), Intel's 2.5D packaging technology, and High-Density Hybrid Bonding (HBI), a next-generation 3D packaging process. Following Lee's appointment, Navid Shahriari, who had been responsible for packaging technologies, will retire from the company.

key_facts.fact: Lee was CEO of SK Hynix from December 2018 through 2022, where he drove development of high-bandwidth memory critical to AI; he then served as president and CEO of SK On (battery) until May 2026, and previously spent about a decade at Intel beginning in 2000 leading 32-nanometer transistor development.
key_facts.excerpt: Lee stepped down as chief executive of SK On at the end of May after 2 1/2 years in the role. Prior to joining the battery maker, he served as chief executive of SK hynix, one of the world's largest memory chip manufacturers, where he played an instrumental role in developing and advancing the company's high-bandwidth memory, a critical component in powering artificial intelligence.

key_facts.fact: Under the new structure, Naga Chandrasekaran continues as EVP of Intel Foundry focused on front-end technology development and manufacturing, including accelerating the ramp of Intel 18A and 14A nodes.
key_facts.excerpt: Naga Chandrasekaran, executive vice president of Intel Foundry, will continue to report to CEO Lip-Bu Tan and lead front-end technology development and front-end manufacturing as the company focuses on accelerating the ramp of Intel 18A, Intel 14A, and future technologies.

key_facts.fact: Intel shares jumped 9% premarket Wednesday after Trump said Apple agreed to work with Intel on US chip design and manufacturing; the Lee hire was Intel's first major leadership move since.
key_facts.excerpt: The leadership change follows President Trump's announcement that Apple Inc. has agreed to work with Intel to design and manufacture chips in the U.S., potentially providing a major boost to Intel's contract manufacturing business.

stories.headline: Meta contracts ~1.6 GW of AI compute from Crusoe across Texas and Missouri data centers

key_facts.fact: Meta is under contract to buy AI computing capacity from data center developer Crusoe at two sites — Childress, Texas and Warrenton, Missouri — for roughly 1.6 gigawatts combined, according to people familiar.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta is under contract to buy computing capacity from Crusoe at two data centers, according to people familiar with the situation. Those operations are located in Childress, Texas, and Warrenton, Missouri. Meta is set to get roughly 1.6 gigawatts of capacity combined across the two sites.

key_facts.fact: Neither the dollar value nor the delivery timeline was disclosed; spokespeople for Meta and Crusoe declined to comment. A single gigawatt is enough to power as many as 750,000 US homes at any given time.
key_facts.excerpt: It wasn't immediately clear how much Meta will be spending or when the computing capacity will be delivered. Spokespeople for Meta and Crusoe declined to comment. A single gigawatt is enough to power as many as 750,000 US homes at any given time.

key_facts.fact: Crusoe, founded in 2018, already has data center deals with Oracle, Microsoft, and Google; earlier this month it said it had contracts for 4.9 GW of capacity, with more than 40 GW in its total project pipeline.
key_facts.excerpt: Crusoe, founded in 2018, specializes in building and running large data centers for AI work. It already has deals with Oracle Corp., Microsoft Corp. and Alphabet Inc.'s Google for three other data center campuses. Crusoe said earlier this month that it had contracts for 4.9 gigawatts' worth of capacity, with more than 40 gigawatts in its total project pipeline.

key_facts.fact: The deal comes after Crusoe was pushed out of development of a major data center in Wyoming after earlier talks with Google fell through, per a prior Bloomberg report.
key_facts.excerpt: The upstart has stumbled in some recent deals. Bloomberg reported last week that Crusoe was being pushed out of development of a data center in Wyoming after earlier deal talks with Google fell through.

stories.headline: Amazon in talks to sell Trainium AI chips outside AWS, taking direct aim at Nvidia

key_facts.fact: Amazon's AI chief Peter DeSantis told Bloomberg from Paris that AWS is in talks to sell its Trainium AI chips for use in third-party data centers; DeSantis declined to name potential customers.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon's AI chief Peter DeSantis told Bloomberg that AWS is in talks to sell its AI chip Trainium to other companies for use in data centers. DeSantis declined to specify which companies could be the buyers of these chips.

key_facts.fact: Rising international demand for sovereign AI infrastructure, particularly in Europe, is a major driver behind the push; DeSantis said AWS sees how businesses build AI infrastructure as 'on the cusp of rapid, wide-ranging change.'
key_facts.excerpt: Peter DeSantis said a major driver behind the push is rising international demand for locally controlled computing resources — particularly in Europe, where regulatory and political pressure has increased calls for sovereign AI infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy in his April shareholder letter said the company's chip business could be a ~$50 billion annual run rate if sold to third parties; current Trainium3 capacity is largely sold out, and the Trainium chip line has generated more than $225 billion in revenue commitments.
key_facts.excerpt: Jassy wrote at the time that selling to both AWS and external customers could push that figure toward $50 billion annually. The Trainium chip line has generated more than $225 billion in revenue commitments, Amazon said in April.

key_facts.fact: Trainium chips are already used through AWS by customers including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Uber; production constraint at TSMC, which has supplanted Apple as the foundry's largest customer, is a key bottleneck for broader sales.
key_facts.excerpt: Trainium chips are already available through AWS and are used by customers including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Uber Technologies, Bloomberg reported.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is currently on a $326 billion revenue run rate; a $50 billion Amazon chip business would be akin to Intel's annual revenue and represent one of the more material challenges to Nvidia's AI chip dominance.
key_facts.excerpt: How much of a challenge could Amazon be to Nvidia? A $50 billion competitor wouldn't exactly tank Nvidia — which is currently on a $326 billion revenue run rate — if it keeps delivering quarters like the last one. But it's akin to Intel's annual revenue.

stories.headline: Samsung Foundry wins talks with AMD, Google, Tesla, Groq as TSMC capacity sells out

key_facts.fact: According to a Nikkei Asia report, a growing list of major chip customers — including AMD, Google, Nvidia-backed Groq, Tesla, and BYD — are in discussions with Samsung Foundry about manufacturing future chips as TSMC's leading-edge capacity is fully booked.
key_facts.excerpt: According to a report from Nikkei Asia, a growing list of major chip customers, including AMD, Google, Nvidia-backed Groq, Tesla, and BYD, are in discussions with Samsung Foundry about manufacturing future chips as demand continues to outstrip TSMC's available capacity.

key_facts.fact: AMD is in talks with Samsung to manufacture certain future CPUs starting in 2028 on Samsung's second-generation 2nm node — its first reported CPU shift to Samsung, with AMD's GPUs remaining at TSMC.
key_facts.excerpt: AMD is reportedly in talks with Samsung about manufacturing certain future CPUs starting in 2028.

key_facts.fact: Google is discussing two separate Samsung engagements: next-gen Axion processors around 2028 and components for its 10th-gen TPU codenamed 'Icefish', co-developed with MediaTek.
key_facts.excerpt: Google is discussing two separate Samsung engagements. One covers its next-generation Axion processors expected around 2028, while the other involves components tied to its 10th-generation Tensor Processing Unit, codenamed Icefish, which is being co-developed with MediaTek.

key_facts.fact: Tesla has confirmed its next-generation AI6 chip will be produced at Samsung's Texas facility; BYD is in talks with Samsung on 2nm and 4nm autonomous driving SoCs; Groq's LP30 AI inference processor will run on Samsung's 4nm node.
key_facts.excerpt: Tesla's A15 chip used in its vehicles and robotics platforms is manufactured by both Samsung and TSMC, while the next-generation A16 will reportedly be exclusively fabricated by the South Korean company at its Texas facility. Groq, an Nvidia-backed startup developing AI accelerators, has also announced that its LP30 AI inference processor will be manufactured by Samsung Foundry on its 4nm process node.

key_facts.fact: AMD stock rose ~3% and Intel ~4% on June 18 as investors reacted to the Samsung-AMD talks; the TSMC capacity squeeze is also driving overflow to Intel Foundry, with reports that Apple could use Intel's 18A-P process for future M7 production in 2027 and Google ordered 3 million TPUs from Intel for 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel Foundry is also benefiting from TSMC's capacity crunch, with reports suggesting Apple could use Intel's 18A-P process for future M7 production in 2027, while Google is said to have ordered 3 million TPUs from Intel for 2028.

stories.headline: Robotics infrastructure startup XDOF emerges from stealth with $70M and open dataset

key_facts.fact: XDOF emerged from stealth with $70 million in funding to build core infrastructure for robot foundation models, including datasets, robotic systems, and software tools for physical AI.
key_facts.excerpt: Robotics training infrastructure startup XDOF said today it has raised $70 million in funding to try to solve one of the biggest challenges in artificial intelligence: teaching machines the skills they need to safely navigate and work in the real world.

key_facts.fact: The round involved Thrive Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Spark Capital, Lux Capital, and WndrCo; XDOF was co-founded by CEO Philipp Wu, CTO Yide (Fred) Shentu, and COO Nemo Jin and traces its roots to a UC Berkeley teleoperation project called GELLO.
key_facts.excerpt: The round involved a number of heavyweight venture capitalists, including Thrive Capital, Spark Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Lux Capital and WndrCo.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the raise, XDOF released ABC-130K, which it calls the largest open-source bimanual robot manipulation dataset — over 130,000 demonstrations across 195 tasks, plus 300 hours of simulations and 100 hours of evaluations — developed with researchers from UC Berkeley, Carnegie Mellon, MIT, and Amazon FAR.
key_facts.excerpt: XDOF released ABC-130K, which it describes as the largest open-source teleoperation dataset, containing more than 130,000 demonstrations across 195 bimanual manipulation tasks developed in collaboration with researchers from UC Berkeley, Carnegie Mellon, MIT and Amazon.

key_facts.fact: XDOF already has roughly 20 active customers, including frontier AI labs, and 60+ employees; it plans to hire a global arm of teleoperators and build proprietary wearable sensors for hand-tracking.
key_facts.excerpt: Although it has been operating under the radar until now, it already has about 20 active customers, including a number of frontier AI labs, and more than 60 employees.

key_facts.fact: The launch comes weeks after OpenAI announced it's reviving its robotics training program, shut down in 2021, amid broader investor enthusiasm for 'physical AI'.
key_facts.excerpt: XDOF's debut comes at a critical juncture, just weeks after OpenAI Group PBC announced it's going to revive its own robotics training program that had been shut down in 2021. That move signified the growing interest in what's known as 'physical AI.'
